questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **meticulous**.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means paying great attention to detail.

questions.question: Choose the word opposite in meaning to **scarce**.
questions.explanation: Scarce means in short supply; its opposite is plentiful.

questions.question: One word for "a person who is new to a subject or skill":
questions.explanation: A novice is a beginner. A veteran or expert has long experience.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **ambiguous**.
options: open to more than one meaning
questions.explanation: An ambiguous statement can be understood in two or more ways.

questions.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to **obsolete**.
questions.explanation: Obsolete means out of date and no longer used.

questions.question: Which word means "to make something less severe"?
questions.explanation: To mitigate is to reduce the seriousness of something. Aggravate is the opposite.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Neither of the two printers in the lab ___ working at present.
questions.explanation: "Neither of" takes a singular verb: is.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She has been working here ___ 2019.
questions.explanation: "Since" goes with a point in time (2019); "for" goes with a period.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The committee ___ its report yesterday.
questions.explanation: "Yesterday" marks a finished past time, so the simple past is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He do not know the answer.
He does not know the answer.
He does not knows the answer.
questions.explanation: After "does not" the main verb stays in its base form: know.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks: He is ___ honest man and ___ M.Sc. graduate.
questions.explanation: "Honest" begins with a vowel sound (silent h), and "M.Sc." is said "em-es-see", so both take "an".

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The manager is senior ___ me in the department.
questions.explanation: Senior, junior, superior and inferior are followed by "to", not "than".

questions.question: Fill in the blank: If I ___ you, I would apply for the post.
questions.explanation: An unreal present condition takes "were" for all persons.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: Each of the students ___ given a certificate.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular, so the verb is singular: was.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Perseverance ends in -ance, from persevere.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Necessary: one c, two s.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Occurrence: double c, double r, and ends in -ence.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: Maintenance drops the "ai" of maintain: maint-e-nance.

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: The clerk typed the letter.
options: The letter is typed by the clerk.
The letter has been typed by the clerk.
The letter was typed by the clerk.
The letter was being typed by the clerk.
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes "was/were + past participle" in the passive.

questions.question: Change to the passive voice: They are repairing the server.
options: The server was repaired by them.
The server is repaired by them.
The server has been repaired by them.
The server is being repaired by them.
questions.explanation: Present continuous becomes "is/are being + past participle".

questions.question: Change to the active voice: The report was submitted by the manager.
options: The manager has submitted the report.
The manager was submitting the report.
questions.explanation: The tense stays the same: simple past.

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: He said, "I am busy."
options: He said that I was busy.
He said that he will be busy.
He said that he was busy.
He said that he had been busy.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the present "am" shifts to the past "was", and "I" becomes "he".

questions.question: Change to indirect speech: She asked, "Where do you live?"
options: She asked where did I live.
She asked where I do live.
She asked that where I lived.
questions.explanation: A reported question uses statement order with no "do", and the tense moves back.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **to bite the bullet**.
options: to face a painful situation bravely
questions.explanation: It means to accept something unpleasant and get on with it.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **a blessing in disguise**.
options: something good that seemed bad at first
questions.explanation: A misfortune that turns out to be beneficial.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **once in a blue moon**.
questions.explanation: It describes something that happens extremely seldom.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: **to pull someone's leg**.
questions.explanation: It means to tease someone playfully, not to harm them.

questions.question: In a letter, "cc" stands for:
questions.explanation: A cc line lists people who receive a copy of the letter.

questions.question: At the foot of a letter, "Encl." indicates:
questions.explanation: Encl. (enclosure) tells the reader that papers are sent with the letter.

questions.question: An NOC issued by an employer is a:
options: certificate that the employer has no objection
questions.explanation: NOC means No Objection Certificate.

questions.question: A circular is:
options: a letter to one person only
a notice sent to many people at once
questions.explanation: A circular carries the same information to a whole group.

questions.passage:
**Read the passage and answer the next 3 questions.**
A good password is long, unique and hard to guess. Many users choose short passwords based on their names or birth dates, which attackers can guess quickly. Using the same password on several sites is also risky, because one leaked password then opens every account. A password manager solves both problems by creating and storing a different strong password for each site. Even so, the manager itself must be protected with a strong master password, and where possible with a second factor such as a code sent to a phone.
questions.question: According to the passage, why is reusing a password risky?
options: One leaked password can open every account that uses it.
questions.explanation: The passage says one leaked password then opens every account.

questions.passage:
**Read the passage and answer the next 2 questions.**
The new library timings take effect from Monday. The reading hall will remain open from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays. It will stay closed on Sundays and public holidays. Borrowing of books will end half an hour before closing time. Members may renew books online up to two times.
questions.question: Until what time can books be borrowed on a weekday?
questions.explanation: The hall closes at 10 p.m. and borrowing ends half an hour earlier.

questions.question: On which day will the reading hall close at 5 p.m.?

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. Therefore the administrator deleted the old logs.
Q. The server stopped responding one morning.
R. The disk had become full of log files.
S. After a restart, everything worked normally again.
questions.explanation: Problem (Q), cause (R), action (P), result (S). "Therefore" needs the cause before it.

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. The meeting will begin sharp at 10 a.m.
Q. Every member is therefore requested to attend on time.
R. A meeting of the purchase committee has been called on Friday.
S. Please bring the latest quotations.
questions.explanation: Announcement (R), time (P), request to be on time (Q, which refers to the time), instruction (S).

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. Soon, it became the main way people pay in shops.
Q. UPI was launched in 2016 to make bank transfers simple.
R. Today, millions of transactions are made through it every day.
S. At first, only a few banks supported it.
questions.explanation: Launch (Q), early stage (S), growth (P), present day (R).

questions.question:
Arrange the sentences in the correct order.

P. The packet is then forwarded to the next router.
Q. A router reads the destination address of each packet.
R. It looks up the best route in its table.
S. This continues until the packet reaches its destination.
questions.explanation: Read address (Q), look up route (R), forward (P), repeat until delivered (S).
